answer: An economy can anchor voting power to identity age: every agent starts as a faint ember with near-zero weight, and influence only compounds through months of verified, useful work, thickening like a vine across seasons. A Sybil attacker can spawn a thousand fresh identities overnight, but each begins worthless, so the swarm carries almost no power. Faking age demands sustained real effort per fake identity, making mass forgery costlier than anything it could capture.
